detail: The ZLB digitised Berlin address and telephone books carry a Solr full-text index, queried directly on 22 September 2026. THE BOOKS PRINT SURNAME FIRST, so every phrase was built that way. Control throughout: "Leibholz Georg" returns 4 and the null string "Leibholz Zqxvwyrk" returns 0. *** AND THE CONTROL IS ALSO THE WARNING: FOUR IS FAR TOO FEW FOR GEORG, *** who is in the directories across years. This index is SPARSE, so a zero from it is weak and a hit from it is solid. Every finding below is a hit.

finding: *** FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ — THE RUN IS LONGER AT BOTH ENDS THAN THIS ARCHIVE HAD ***
detail: Row 251 had him at Schwabstraße 4, Reinickendorf, 1961 to 1970, a man who retired between 1959 and 1961. THE FULL RUN IS 1957 TO 1973-74. 1957: "Leipholz Friedrich ANGESTELLTER, Tgl" — Tegel. 1959: the same. 1961: "PENSIONÄR, Rei 1" — Reinickendorf. 1963, 1964, 1967 ("Pens 51 Schwabstr 4"), 1970. THEN THE TELEPHONE BOOKS: 1970-71, "Leipholz Friedrich 49 80 11, 51 Schwabstr. 4"; and 1973-74, "Leipholz Friedrich 4 91 82 51, 51 Schwabstr. 4".

finding: *** TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS, AND THE ARCHIVE IS NOT CLAIMING WHY ***
detail: 49 80 11 in 1970-71 and 4 91 82 51 in 1973-74, at the same flat. Berlin was lengthening subscriber numbers across exactly that period, so a renumbering of one line is the ordinary explanation — but 49 80 11 does not expand tidily into 4 91 82 51, and this archive has been caught once today making a hard reading fit a hypothesis. RECORDED AS TWO NUMBERS AT ONE ADDRESS.

finding: what the new end date is worth
detail: The same method that bracketed ERNA LEIPHOLZ — present in the telephone book until 1979-80 and gone from 1980-81 — now brackets Friedrich at the other end of the shelf. HE IS THERE IN 1973-74. The volumes after it were not checked in this pass, so his disappearance is not yet bracketed and his death is not dated. THAT IS THE NEXT STEP AND IT IS CHEAP.

finding: *** AND IT JOINS ROW 250 TO ROW 251, WHICH WERE SEPARATE ROWS ***
detail: In 1957 and 1959 the directory prints them together, Friedrich first and then the repeat-dash for the same surname: "Leipholz Friedrich Angest Tgl Berlin — KLARA PUTZMACHERIN SW 29 DIEFFENBACH[STRASSE]". That is row 250's Klara, in row 251's listing, in the same two years. The adjacency is only alphabetical and proves no kinship — BUT IT DOES SHOW THESE TWO ARE THE WHOLE OF THE LEIPHOLZ NAME IN BERLIN IN THOSE YEARS, which is what makes either of them worth following.

finding: # ---------------- WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ, TRACED ACROSS TWENTY-THREE YEARS ----------------
*** THE CAREER, FROM THE DIRECTORIES THEMSELVES ***
detail: 1912 and 1910 in the trade sections; 1920 "Leibholz, William, GEN. DIREKT., STADTRAT"; 1921 "General[direktor], Berlin-Wilmersdorf"; 1925 "Kaufmann, Direktor, Berlin-Grunewald" and at Sigmaringer Str. 30; 1929 "FABRIKANT, Grunewald, Königs[allee]" three times; 1933 "STADTRAT UND FABRIKBESITZER" four times. A man who rises from merchant to city councillor and factory owner.

KÖNIGSALLEE 29, BERLIN-GRUNEWALD, in 1932 and 1933. And in a 1932 motor register: "1974 P Leibholz, William, Grunewald, Königsallee 29, HORCH 65" — a large and expensive German car. This is a wealthy household.

Hits run 1910, 1912, 1913, 1914, 1920, 1921, 1925, 1929, 1932, 1933 — AND NOTHING AFTER. 1933 is the year Jewish officials were removed from German public life, and a Stadtrat is a public office. THE ARCHIVE IS NOT CLAIMING THAT IS WHY. A sparse index, a death, a move or a changed entry would each produce the same silence.

finding: *** HE IS NOT IN THE GEDENKBUCH, AND THAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS SAID ***
detail: The memorial book holds three men of the name: WILHELM b. 28.12.1890 Glowitz, of Neukölln; WILHELM b. 15.12.1904 Tempelburg, of Friedrichshain; and WILHELM WILLI b. 30.12.1887 Berlin, of Friedrichshain. NONE FITS. A man who was already Generaldirektor and Stadtrat by 1920 was born around 1870, not 1887 or 1890 or 1904 — and none of the three lived in Grunewald. So the Königsallee William is not among the murdered.

finding: what row 242 actually asked, and it is still open
detail: Whether he is the father of JOACHIM PETER LEIBHOLZ, born Berlin 20 August 1903, who reached Melbourne in June 1939 and whose Victorian death index names his father as WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ and his mother as NANETTE NÉE NETTER. A wealthy Berlin Stadtrat of exactly the right generation fits — AND NOTHING JOINS THEM. "Netter Nanette" returns ZERO in these books, and the eight pages where Leibholz and Netter both appear are a directory of thousands of names, where sharing a page means nothing. WHAT WOULD JOIN THEM is Joachim Peter's Berlin birth entry of 1903.

finding: # ---------------- AND TWO THAT CAME BACK EMPTY ----------------
Isidor Rosenberg of Schlochau — not found
detail: Rosenberg Isidor returns 12, and every one is a company registration — Hermann Rosenberg GmbH, Gebr. Rosenberg, Max Rosenberg GmbH, a Rosenberg-Kleider-Werkstätte. NONE IS THE SCHLOCHAU ISIDOR, father of Jenny née Rosenberg. Rosenberg is among the commonest Jewish surnames in Berlin and a forename search cannot separate him.

finding: Spier at Treuchtlinger Straße 4 — not found
detail: Spier AND "Treuchtlinger" returns 3 pages, and on none of them is a Spier AT that address: the Spiers found are a Konfitüren-Geschäft in W 30, a Fritz Spier of Schöneberg, and a Friedrich and Liselotte Spier of Dianastraße. THE CO-OCCURRENCE IS PAGE-LEVEL, NOT ADDRESS-LEVEL, which is the same trap as the two Lutherstraßen. The Spier household Jacob Leibholz lodged with at Treuchtlingerstr. 4 is not reachable this way.
